intro: Professionals and everyday users convert pounds per cubic foot (lb/ft³) to kilograms per cubic meter (kg/m³) when working across imperial and si standards in materials science specifications, concrete and soil compaction testing, chemical solution density, and buoyancy calculations. One pound per cubic foot equals 16.018463 kilograms per cubic meter, while 1 kilogram per cubic meter equals 0.062428 pounds per cubic foot. Whether you are verifying density & concentration specifications on imported equipment, cross-checking technical datasheets, or scaling practical measurements, this converter applies the exact NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 reference relationship with instant precision.

mistakesAndEdgeCases.title: Exact NIST Factor vs. Early Rounding Drift
items: The exact conversion factor from Pound per Cubic Foot to Kilogram per Cubic Meter is 16.01846337, derived from the 1959 International Yard and Pound Agreement (1 inch = 25.4 mm, 1 lb = 0.45359237 kg).

In structural engineering, CNC machining, or bulk inventory totals, rounding the multiplier to 2 decimal places too early can introduce cumulative tolerance errors; always compute with the full factor and round only the final displayed figure.

faqs.question: How many kilograms per cubic meter (kg/m³) are in 1 pound per cubic foot (lb/ft³)?
faqs.answer: There are 16.01846337 kilograms per cubic meter (kg/m³) in 1 pound per cubic foot (lb/ft³), which rounds to 16.0185 kg/m³ for everyday calculations. Conversely, 1 kilogram per cubic meter equals 0.062428 pounds per cubic foot.

faqs.question: How do I convert pounds per cubic foot to kilograms per cubic meter (lb/ft³ to kg/m³)?
faqs.answer: To convert pounds per cubic foot to kilograms per cubic meter, use the formula: kg/m³ = lb/ft³ × 16.01846337. For example, converting 10 lb/ft³ gives 160.1846 kg/m³.

faqs.question: What is 10 pounds per cubic foot in kilograms per cubic meter?
faqs.answer: 10 pounds per cubic foot (lb/ft³) equals exactly 160.1846 kilograms per cubic meter (kg/m³) using standard NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 conversion factors.
